instruction.text: Spell the name of the river.

atoms.word: S e v e r n

feedback.finish: The River Severn is the longest river in the UK.

instruction.text: Trace the river’s route, starting at Plynlimon.

feedback.finish: The River Severn’s source is an area of boggy ground high up in the Welsh mountains. It flows for 220 miles through the English cities of Shrewsbury, Worcester and Gloucester. Its estuary opens up into the Bristol Channel.

The River Severn is prone to flooding. One of the worst recorded floods took place in July 2007, when 90 mm of rain fell in Gloucester, causing the river to flood onto its floodplains. Local communities were left without water for a long time afterwards.

instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: The Severn Estuary flows into the Bristol Channel, which is located between South-West England and South Wales. This then connects to the Atlantic Ocean, so the estuary sees high tidal waves.
When the tide rises, water is pushed up from the estuary into the narrow river channel, which creates a wave called the Severn Bore. This wave is sometimes high enough for surfing!

atoms.a: What does the Severn Estuary flow into?

b: ++a big wave created by the rising sea tide
a boring part of the river

instruction.text: Select the picture of a wetland.

finish.sound: The River Severn’s wetlands, an area of marshy land, act as a habitat for many bird species, such as geese and sandpipers.
text: The River Severn’s wetlands (an area of marshy land) act as a habitat for many bird species, such as geese and sandpipers.

instruction.text: Listen and select the correct answer.

atoms.a: What is being done to protect the Severn and its wildlife?

b.sound: Laws have been passed to limit the amount of waste that can be put into the river.
Plastic pollution and sewage from factories helps keep the river clean.

feedback.end: The Severn Estuary is a special area of conservation, where all plants and animals living there are protected.

feedback.finish: The Severn Estuary widens dramatically and is home to the Severn Bridge, which spans from Gloucestershire in England to Monmouthshire in Wales.
